title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is continuing the 'Longue Marche' discussion of the outer Galois action on the fundamental group of X = M_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, with its S_3 symmetry. On the previous page (282) the extension of Gamma (essentially Gal(Qbar/Q), times S_3) by \hat M is compared with an extension G~_{p,sigma} of \hat Z^* x S_3 by \hat M coming from the Fermat tower. \hat M is an abelian profinite group, presumably the abelianized geometric pi_1. That extension splits, with a unique \hat M-conjugacy class of splittings. This pulls back to a canonical (but not unique) conjugacy class of splittings of \tilde M -> Gamma. Equivalently, it gives a canonical class of liftings of the Gamma-action to the covering X_0.

Top of this page: the end of that sentence. The lifting yields a commutative diagram, so that the 'dessin' (Galois-stable covering) of (M_{0,3,Qbar}, S_3) corresponding to the extension is isomorphic to the unique covering (of U_{0,3,Qbar}) considered earlier.

Main part: back to 'the general duality situation'. Data:
- an abelian group M with an action of Gamma, encoded by an extension 1 -> M -> \tilde M -> Gamma -> 1;
- a Gamma-equivariant affine M-torsor E (called Theta_{\tilde M}), i.e. a diagram (281) mapping \tilde M to the affine group of E.

The image of \tilde M in Aff(E) = M ⋊ Aut(M) is a quotient \tilde{\tilde M} of \tilde M. Since M acts faithfully by translations, M injects into it. This gives the exact sequence (283):
1 -> M -> \tilde{\tilde M} -> \tilde{\tilde Gamma} -> 1,
where \tilde{\tilde Gamma} is the image of Gamma in Aut(M) (284), so it acts faithfully on M.

Conversely, the quotients of \tilde M arising this way are arbitrary, subject only to two conditions: M injects, and the quotient group acts faithfully on M. A kernel N with N ∩ M = 1 automatically centralizes M, so it lies over ker(Gamma -> Aut M).

Next page: (283) is split. The torsor gives an M-equivariant map E -> Scind(\tilde{\tilde M}), sending x to the stabilizer of x. Two points x, y have the same image iff y - x ∈ M^Gamma. Hence E -> Scind is injective iff M^Gamma = 0. In that case E is identified with one M-conjugacy class of splittings.

This is the standard dictionary: equivariant affine torsors correspond to conjugacy classes of splittings of the semidirect product with the faithful quotient of Gamma, with classes in H^1. Grothendieck uses it to pass between Galois-equivariant torsors (e.g. from the Fermat tower) and splittings of the arithmetic fundamental group extension.
errors: Minor slip: 'Ces quotients \tilde{\tilde M} de M' should be 'de \tilde M'; quotients of \tilde M are meant.

Implicit hypotheses are not stated on this page: M must be abelian (the next page uses additive notation y - x ∈ M), and the kernel of \tilde M -> \tilde{\tilde M} must be normal and meet M trivially. Neither is wrong in context.

ideas.what: The image of an extension \tilde M of Gamma by an abelian M in the affine group of an equivariant M-torsor is a quotient \tilde{\tilde M} = M ⋊ (image of Gamma in Aut M). Such quotients are characterised by M injecting and the quotient acting faithfully on M.
ideas.modern_name: Affine group / semidirect product; torsors vs. splittings of group extensions
ideas.where_published: Similar torsor/splitting formalism appears in SGA 1 and Grothendieck's general nonabelian cohomology viewpoint; this exact formulation is unknown to me.

ideas.what: Using the Fermat-tower extension (split, with a unique conjugacy class of splittings) to obtain a canonical class of liftings of the Galois action to the covering of M_{0,3} with S_3 symmetry, i.e. an isomorphism of 'dessins'.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the metabelian/abelianized fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points; Ihara's Fermat-tower / Jacobi-sum power series
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly restates the standard equivalence between Gamma-equivariant affine torsors and conjugacy classes of splittings of the associated (faithful-quotient) semidirect product. The arithmetic thread it serves (Fermat tower splitting the abelianized Galois extension for M_{0,3}) belongs to Ihara's well-documented work. Nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'définit une quotient / de \tilde M' should read 'définit un quotient \tilde{\tilde M} de \tilde M'; the \tilde{\tilde M} written above the line is inserted at the slash.
In (284) and the following line the subject is \tilde{\tilde Gamma} (not Gamma): '\tilde{\tilde Gamma} s'identifie à l'image de Gamma dans Aut(M)'.
'sous la condition que M ↪ \tilde{\tilde M} soit injectif' is better read as '(... M ↪ \tilde{\tilde M} est injectif), et ...'; a struck-out 'injectif' is replaced inline.
Line 2 likely reads 'qui au dessin de U_{0,3,Qbar} soit isomorphe au rev. ∃! envisagé plus haut'.
